answer: Practically, the chain should stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because oasis only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, karst is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
